$comment: Each row is one deliberate defect. tools/mutate.js applies it to a throwaway copy of the repository and runs the full suite. A mutation that still passes is a SURVIVOR and fails the build; a `find` that no longer matches exactly once is STALE and also fails, because it means the code moved and the row stopped describing anything.

mutations.find:
local src = source
        if type(src) ~= 'number' or src <= 0 then
            return
        end
mutations.replace:
local src = source
        if type(src) ~= 'number' then
            return
        end
mutations.why: Drop the `src <= 0` half of the guard. `source` is 0 for a server-side trigger and -1 for a scheduled one, so a net handler that accepts them can be invoked by anything that can raise the event locally, with no player behind it.
Make the default rate limit effectively unlimited. The limiter still exists and still works; it simply never refuses, which is the failure mode a limit that defaults to permissive always produces.

mutations.find:
local CELL = CisGrid.CELL
local STRIDE = CisGrid.STRIDE
mutations.replace:
local _MIGRATION = 'CREATE TABLE cis_libs_x (id INT)'

local CELL = CisGrid.CELL
local STRIDE = CisGrid.STRIDE
mutations.why: A shipped file that creates a table. The whole zero-tables promise, and the thing that makes a free library safe to install. A string literal is the realistic form: this is what a convenience helper looks like after someone pastes in a schema.
A shipped file calling a third-party resource by name. cis_libs reaches other resources only through the capability registry; a literal export call is the boundary being broken by a different route.
A shipped file writing to disk outside the reviewed allow-list. Already allow-listed at two sites, so this also proves the allow-list is a list and not a blanket.

mutations.find:
if src ~= 0 then
        print('cis_libs: cis_force_unregister is a server console command. '
mutations.replace:
if false then
        print('cis_libs: cis_force_unregister is a server console command. '
mutations.why: Remove the source check from the one console command that removes a capability. The restricted flag stays, so this is precisely the belt surviving the braces: anything that can get a player id in front of the handler -- a console that forwards a src, or a restricted flag that is not what it was assumed to be -- can strip `security`, `database` or `framework` from a running server.

mutations.find:
-- through `deliverNotification` like its twin.
    return deliverNotification(src, message, kind)
mutations.replace:
-- through `deliverNotification` like its twin.
    TriggerClientEvent('cis_libs:client:showNotification', src, message, kind)
mutations.why: Skip the shared guard on the fallback path. `Notify` with no framework behind it and `NotifyClient` are the same act, and this is the shape they had before: the bounded path was the rarer one, so a server with no framework installed had the unbounded one.

Remove the connected-player check from the shared notify guard. A plausible server id is not a player, so without this the export reports success and fires at somebody who has already left -- the worst of both, because it looks delivered and reaches nobody.

mutations.find:
if item.payload.target == src then
            doomed[#doomed + 1] = key
        end
    end
    for i = 1, #doomed do
        local item = pending.items[doomed[i]]
mutations.replace:
if false then
            doomed[#doomed + 1] = key
        end
    end
    for i = 1, #doomed do
        local item = pending.items[doomed[i]]
mutations.why: Remove the playerDropped rejection. Every server-to-client await aimed at a player who has just left then waits out the full CallbackTimeout -- 10 seconds and a parked live coroutine per outstanding call -- and is reported as a generic 'timeout', so the caller is told the client was slow about a client that is gone.

mutations.find:
if allowAnyResource() then
        applyPosture('permissive', 'Security.AllowAnyResource is set')
        return
    end
mutations.why: Make an empty AuthorizedResources permissive again -- the exact behaviour DEC-2 removes. Every resource on the server regains the right to add, break and rewrite every door and every synced entity, on a server whose operator was told the gate was closed. The refusal itself is unchanged, so nothing about the shape of the answer gives it away.

mutations.find:
for id, record in pairs(records) do
        if record.owner == resource then
            remove(id)
        end
    end
end)
mutations.replace:
for id, record in pairs(records) do
        if true then
            remove(id)
        end
    end
end)
mutations.why: Remove the owner check on the stop sweep, so any resource stopping takes every OTHER resource's records with it. This is the D-03 P0 in its current form: not a silent table wipe this time, but the same player-visible harm -- every synced prop on the server disappears the moment any one consumer restarts, and every client that was told about one is left holding it.

mutations.find:
if peeked.payload.target ~= src then
        return
    end
mutations.why: Take the pending callback entry without the ownership check. Keys are sequential integers, so a client can name any of them; without this the caller destroys someone else's pending request.

mutations.find:
local owner = invokingResource()
        or (type(provider) == 'table' and provider.resource)
        or 'cis_libs'
mutations.replace:
local owner = (type(provider) == 'table' and provider.resource)
        or (type(provider) == 'string' and provider)
        or 'cis_libs'
mutations.why: Take the capability owner from an argument instead of the invoker, which lets a resource claim ownership of a slot it did not register.
Remove the length cap on a client notification. An unbounded string crossing to every client is the cheapest way to make every player pay for one caller's mistake.
